name: Leverage Points
subject: quantum-computing
subjectTitle: A Skeptic's Guide to Quantum Computing

lesson.title: Where to Push on a System That Won't Budge
lesson.summary: Donella Meadows' leverage points framework ranks the places you can intervene in a system from weakest, adjusting numbers and parameters, to strongest, shifting the goals and paradigms the system is built to serve, and applying it to quantum computing suggests funding levels, the lever most people reach for first, are actually one of the weaker points available.
lesson.body:
This section has built up a specific diagnosis: quantum computing's public narrative is dominated by strong reinforcing loops, hype, sunk cost, geopolitical competition, paired with a balancing loop too weak to keep them tethered to physical reality. The natural next question is where you would actually push to fix that. The systems analyst Donella Meadows spent much of her career on exactly this question, and her essay on leverage points, places to intervene in a system, remains the standard reference for thinking about it. Her central finding, based on decades of work modeling systems from commodity markets to global resources, is that not all intervention points are equally powerful, and the one people reach for first is usually one of the weakest available.

Meadows arranged interventions roughly from weakest to strongest. Near the bottom sit numbers and parameters, tax rates, subsidy levels, or in this book's context funding amounts, easy to adjust but usually absorbed without changing underlying behavior. Above that sit buffer and stock sizes, the physical structure of how things flow through the system, feedback delays, then the strength of balancing loops, then reinforcing loops. Higher still sit information flows, who has access to what data and how visibly, the system's formal and informal rules, the power to self-organize, meaning who may change the rules, and near the top, the goals the system is oriented toward and the paradigm, the shared assumptions those goals arise from.

Applying this to quantum computing is clarifying. The instinctive response to hype or sunk cost escalation is a parameter level move: fund more oversight, cut a budget line. Meadows' framework predicts, correctly in most documented cases, that such moves get absorbed with little lasting effect, since the reinforcing loops driving the behavior stay untouched. A rules level intervention, requiring prominent claims be pre-registered against a defined benchmark, sits higher. An information flow intervention, changing how prominently corrective findings circulate relative to announcements, sits higher still, mapping directly onto the missing balancing loop: strengthening it is largely an information problem, not a funding one. Highest would be a goal level shift, moving the system's implicit objective from fundable headlines toward verified capability, a far larger change than adjusting any single number.

A concrete comparison makes this tangible. Increasing an oversight committee's budget is a parameter level change: cheap, reversible, and historically not very effective at changing what gets funded. Establishing a neutral, audited public benchmark that any hardware claim must clear before being reported as a record is at once a rules and an information change, altering which claims can even trigger the next round of the hype loop. Meadows' framework predicts the second, though harder to build, would do far more to restrain the loops covered earlier in this section.

Meadows herself noted the catch: leverage points get harder to use as they get more powerful. Changing a funding number takes one signature. Changing a field's shared paradigm, its assumption that impressive announcements measure progress, requires changing minds across an entire community, which resists precisely because the change is powerful. The framework promises no easy fix, only an honest map of where the real fix would have to happen, a fitting close before this section turns to named voices who have pushed, with only partial success, against these deeper levers for years.
